father_note: Nessa, your mother is Sela — she made a hard choice in a hard year, and that means something; keep her close. Vela gave me food when she had no reason to, and I have not forgotten it, so watch her and learn what quiet generosity looks like before you decide it's weakness. Fear Mako most: he has strength, he has food, and he only started speaking when he had already decided something. Trust no one who has not paid a cost to stand beside you — words are free, and this village proved that to me the year it put nine bodies between me and one man's food.

memory_raw.text: Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.

Sela. I have two food and you have none — take one, but listen to me first: Mako is sitting on seven and hasn't said a word to anyone, and that's not patience, that's a man who's already made a decision.

You're my blood, Nessa, and that means something real in a place like this — not words, real. I've got ten food and I'll teach you what I know about when to take and when to wait, but first I need to know you understand what this village will do to someone who looks weak.

I understand it. I've watched Taric hold one food for three years running and nobody trades with him anymore — they don't fear him, they just don't think of him. But I want to know what you see in Mako, because he's not weak and he's not talking, and that worries me more than anyone who is.

Eron, Mako has seven food and he's said nothing to anyone all year — that's not a man being careful, that's a man who's already counted the board and likes what he sees. Watch yourself around him, and don't let him catch you alone.

You've only got two food heading into next year — that's not enough if the pile comes up short again. Bram will give to me before he gives to you, but I'll make sure some of it reaches you; that's not charity, that's blood. Just stay visible, stay useful, and give Mako nothing to count against you.
Eron, you've got one food right now and that's a thin rope to cross a winter on — I'm giving you one of mine, and I need you to eat it before anyone tallies what you're carrying.
You're at two now, which is better — but keep your head down this year, don't give anyone a reason to look your way. If the pile comes up light again, you come to me first, not Sela, not Bram, me.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Eron, the pile went dry before I could reach it — I'm sitting on four food and you've got nine, which means this year you're the one who looks worth watching. Don't let anyone see you spending freely, and if Mako starts talking to you, you come find me before you answer him.

Nine doesn't make me safe, it makes me a target — I've been watching Mako all year and he's already got six, which means if he decides to move on someone he's got the strength for it and half an excuse. You're right that I'll come to you first, but Nessa, I need you to tell me straight: is Bram watching my count, because if he sees me sitting heavy while you're at four, he might think I'm hoarding from his daughter and that's a different kind of trouble.

Bram counts everything, but he's not going to come at you over food when you're his son and I'm his daughter — what he'd see is family holding, not hoarding. What I'd worry about is Mako seeing those nine and deciding you're worth the risk of a fight before anyone else can stop him; you're strong but he's stronger, and he's got Ryn running near him lately which means he might not come alone.

Ryn near Mako is the piece I didn't have — that's two of the strongest in this village moving together, and if they decide to make an example of someone it won't be a fair fight. I'm going to find Kael and Roan before nightfall and make sure they know what we're looking at; nine food means nothing if I'm standing alone when Mako decides the count favors him.

Kael and Roan are the right people to tell, but don't frame it as asking for protection — frame it as giving them information, because men who feel useful are more reliable than men who feel needed. And Eron — give one food to Sela before anyone else sees your count; nine draws eyes, eight draws fewer.

Sela gets one before the sun moves — but I want to know if you trust Kael the way I do, because if I'm bringing him and Roan into the same breath about Mako, I need to know you won't see that as me leaning on your father's enemies.

Kael's not Bram's enemy — they're two careful men who've never had reason to test each other, and that's different. I trust Kael because he said hard things when it cost him, same reason I trust Roan, and neither of those has anything to do with Bram. Bring them in.

Then it's settled — Kael and Roan before nightfall, and one food to Sela now. But Nessa, while I've still got you: Ryn and Mako together worries me more than anything else in this village right now, and I want to know if you've heard anything from Bram's side about what those two have said to each other, because your father listens to things I can't reach.

Bram hasn't said anything to me about Ryn and Mako specifically, but he doesn't have to — if those two had spoken, Bram would have gone quiet in a particular way and he hasn't, which means either they haven't talked yet or they were careful enough that even he missed it. Either way, the silence itself is the warning: a man like Mako doesn't need words to build an alliance, he just needs someone to stand still long enough to be counted as his.

Then I'll treat the silence as the warning it is and move before it becomes something louder. One last thing while I've got you alone, Nessa — you're four food and I'm nine, and you've given me more than I've given back; if the year turns sideways and you need one, it's already yours.

Hold it — don't make that offer where anyone could hear you later and count it as debt between us, but I'm glad you said it, and I won't forget it. Go find Kael and Roan before the light changes, and keep your face easy when you do it — men who look worried when they're looking for allies already look like they're losing.

Nessa, you're sitting on four food and you gave three away to Eron last year — I watched it happen and I didn't say anything then, but I'm saying it now. Eron is Sela's blood, not yours, and generosity in a lean village gets remembered as weakness before it gets remembered as kindness.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

Eron, Nessa — I've got two food and you're the only two in this village I'd spend either one on without thinking. Pile's empty, Mako's still sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone today, and Bram's got four which means he's watching Nessa the way a man watches his investment. Tell me what you each have and we'll figure out how to make sure all three of us eat before the year closes.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

Eron, you've been feeding me half the year out of your own stores — I need to know what that's left you with, because I won't watch my son starve to keep me upright. And Nessa, Bram's put a lot of food your way since you were born, and I want to know whether that feels like a father to you or like a man who expects you to remember it.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

Eron's got nine food — I can see that number same as anyone — and I won't pretend it doesn't ease something in my chest, though I want to hear from his own mouth how he got there. Nessa, four food is yours, and you came into this world three days old with Bram already counting you as something he built — I need to know if you've decided what you think of that, because how you answer it shapes what the three of us can trust each other with.

Eron gave back to Sela and Roan both — he's not just taking, he's building something, and I'd rather know where that lands before I decide he's a drain. But I hear you on the food, and I won't pretend four is comfortable when Mako's walking around with six and nobody's said a word to him about it.
Mako's the one I'd be watching if I were you — six food, no kin, and the strongest arms in this village outside of Dell, and Dell at least has Ryn and Dav to answer to. What's his angle?

Nessa, I'm still waiting on your read of Mako — but while I'm thinking about it, four food between the two of us isn't much of a wall if he decides this is the year he stops being quiet. You should be sleeping closer to me, not spreading food around people whose blood doesn't run yours.

Mako hasn't moved in six years because he's waiting for someone else to thin the herd first — that's not patience, that's strategy, and a man with that much food and no attachments is one bad year away from deciding he doesn't need to wait anymore. You're right that four food isn't a wall, but the answer isn't just me sleeping closer to you — the answer is we look like more than two people when he's doing the counting.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
The pile came up empty again and I've got two food going into the year's end — you two all right on what you're holding?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, I saw you gave me another food — I won't forget that, but don't leave yourself short on my account. Eron, what are you sitting at right now?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Eron's got five and I've got three now — pile's empty so we're all eating what we carry. Nessa, you're at one, that's thin going into year-end; I can spare you one if it means you wake up next year.

Sela just had Mako's child — which means he's not without attachments anymore, and that changes the count. A man with a daughter looks different than a man alone, and I'd rather know whose side Sela's on now before we decide what Mako's angle is.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're at two now — that's still thinner than I'd like, and if you're one short by year-end you won't wake up. I've got four; I can give you one more and still eat.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're sitting at three now and Eron I see you've been moving food around — where are you landing? I need to know we're all going to eat before I stop counting.
Nessa draws Roan aside to talk.
Nessa: have a child with me — I'll put in 1 of 3 food.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Nessa gathers Eron, Zinn to talk.

Eron, you're at four food and Zinn's at nine — between the three of us we're sitting heavier than most, but I want to know what either of you heard near the pile this morning, because Kael walked away with three and didn't say a word to anyone about it, and that's new for him.

Kael's been quiet all year and then takes three without a word — that's a man deciding he's done asking permission. I didn't hear anything near the pile, but I've got eyes: Dell's sitting at eight, I'm at nine, and if Kael starts thinking about what's heavy he'll look our way before he looks at Roan.

Kael taking three doesn't read to me as aggression — he's old and careful, and a man who counts his years knows he can't afford to come up short. What I'd watch is whether he talks to Taric before nightfall, because those two have moved quiet together before. Zinn, you're nine food and Mako's your blood — I need to know whether he sees that as his food or yours, because if he does, your count is the thing in this village most likely to start something.

Mako's given me food twice this year and asked nothing back — that reads like a man who sees my food as ours, not his, but I hear you, Eron, and I'll talk to him before he gets any ideas about counting my pile. What I know is Dell's sitting at eight and she's been feeding Ryn all year, so if Kael's looking for a soft target it won't be me — it'll be whatever pair he thinks he can split.

Dell feeding Ryn all year with eight food and no obvious source — that's not generosity, that's investment, and I want to know what Ryn's supposed to return. Zinn, talk to Mako before he starts counting your pile as his, and Nessa, you're closer to Bram's ear than either of us — has he said anything about Dell or Ryn that would tell us what that pair is building?

Bram hasn't named Dell or Ryn directly, but last year when Dav moved on Esa and those two joined in without a word of warning, Bram went very still — and that kind of still from him means he's filing it away, not dismissing it. What Dell and Ryn built isn't food, it's a habit of moving together, and that's worth more than eight in a fight. Eron, you're the one with something to offer Roan right now — go find him before Dell does.

Nessa's right that Roan's available and Eron's got food to offer, but Roan's got nothing and nothing to lose — a man like that is as likely to go with whoever asks last as whoever asks first, so don't make a deal you can't keep. What I want to know before any of us approaches anyone is whether Dell already knows our numbers, because if she's been watching the pile as close as she's been feeding Ryn, she counted us this morning same as we counted her.

Dell counted us this morning, same as we counted her — that's not a question, that's the shape of things. What matters is whether she sees us as three separate counts or one number, and right now we haven't given her a reason to see us as one. Eron, before you go to Roan, I want the three of us to be clear on what we're offering him and what we're not, because a promise made in a hurry is the kind Roan will hold you to when it's inconvenient.

If we're going to Roan, the offer is simple: one food now, and if trouble comes his way we stand with him — no more than that, because a bigger promise just tells him we're desperate. Eron, you carry it; you've given food before and it won't read as a bid for something.

Zinn's right on the shape of it — one food, one promise, nothing that sounds like we're building something. But Eron, when you go to him, don't mention Mako or Zinn's count; the less Roan knows about what we're holding, the less he has to trade away to someone else later.
Eron, go to Roan before the day gets long — and keep it short, one food and we stand with you, nothing else. I'll find Mako and settle what's mine before he starts counting it as his.
Eron, go now while Roan's still alone — and when you come back, tell me what his face does when you hand it to him, because a man's face on a gift tells you more than the words he puts around it.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Pile's gone and I've got two food — enough to eat, not enough to breathe easy. Eron, Nessa, Zinn: tell me what you're each holding, because I need to know my blood is fed before I start counting anyone else.

Three food, and I'm holding it. Eron, don't answer that out loud — what we carry isn't something Sela needs to worry about, because she's fed, and the less any number gets spoken, the less it travels.

Nessa's right that numbers travel, but I'm your mother and I need to know — not to take, to plan. Zinn, you and Eron can stay quiet if you want, but at least tell me you're both above one food so I can stop doing the math in my chest.
I'm above one, Sela — well above. Don't do the math in your chest; do it here with us where it's useful.

Zinn, "well above" is the kind of answer that keeps me up at night more than a number would — I'm not asking so I can worry, I'm asking so that if Kael or Mako or anyone else moves this year, I know what the four of us can put together before we have to decide anything. Eron, same question, same reason.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Eron's sitting on seven and I can see that same as anyone who's been watching — what I can't see is where his head is after giving Roan two food today before he answered me. Eron, I'm not counting against you, I'm counting with you: if Kael took three from the pile and Zinn took three and neither of them is blood, that's a conversation waiting to happen before they decide they took the wrong amount.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Eron's given me two food while I was sitting here — I see that, and I'm not going to pretend it doesn't answer part of my question. What I need now is the same from Zinn: a number, not a direction, because I can't plan with a compass when I need a map.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Zinn, Roan, Vela, Ryn, Mako, Nessa, Sela, Esa, Eron, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 705).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 8: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).

Nessa, the pile's gone and Dell just took three of it — same as me, which means she's not pretending anymore. You've got two food and I've got five; stay close to me this year and don't give any of it away until we know which way Mako's going to lean now that he's got five himself.

Dell taking three and you taking three in the same year — that's not coincidence, that's two people who've decided the pretending is over. I'll stay close, but Bram, last year the whole village stood against you over Vela and I was one of them — if you're planning something this year I need to know before it happens, not while I'm deciding which side to stand on.

You were right to stand against me on Vela — I went alone when I shouldn't have, and that's a mistake I won't repeat. What I'm planning this year is nothing until I know where Mako stands, because five food and eighty-three strength moving in the wrong direction changes every calculation I've got. I need you telling me what you hear from Sela and Zinn — that's what staying close means.

Sela won't tell me anything she thinks reaches you, and Zinn's Mako's blood — so what I can give you from that side is limited, and you should know that going in. What I can do is watch how Mako moves around Zinn, because a man shows his real count in what he gives his daughter, not what he says to anyone.

That's a better angle than trying to read what he says — watch what he moves, not what he speaks. If he's feeding Zinn heavy this year before things get tight, he thinks he can afford to, which means he's counting on taking more later. Tell me the moment you see that shift.

I will — but there's something else that sits wrong with me about this year already, and it's not Mako. Dell walked away with three food and Ryn is beside her, and those two moved as one when Dav hit Esa without anyone asking them to — they don't need words to act together, they already proved that. If Dell decides to move on someone with Ryn at her shoulder, the math on that is ugly for anyone standing alone.

Dell and Ryn together is a hundred and fifty-six strength before anyone else moves, and I'm not standing in front of that alone — which means the only question that matters is whether Mako's on our side of that problem or theirs when it lands. If he's feeding Zinn steady this year and not building toward anyone, he might be the wall we need.

Mako as a wall only works if he sees Dell as a threat before she moves, and right now he's got no reason to — she's never looked his way. The thing that might turn him is if he figures out that eleven food in Dell's hands is a different kind of power than five in his.

Eleven food is exactly the number I'd plant in his head — not as a warning about me, but as a mirror showing him what she could do if she decided five in his hands was worth having. You're the one he'll hear it from without suspecting a count behind it.

I'll do it, but I want something clear between us first — if I go to Mako and plant that number, I'm the one standing in the open, and I need to know that if Dell ever traces it back, I'm not standing there alone.
You won't be standing alone — if Dell traces it back to you, she traces it back to me, and that's where I want her eyes. You're my blood and I don't leave blood exposed.
Then I'll go to Mako before the day gets long — but Bram, I'm not just planting a number, I'm watching what he does with it, and if he flinches or goes quiet, you'll know before anyone else does.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Dell, Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

The pile's gone again before half of us got near it, and the two who ate best — Bram and Mako — both took more than their share while the rest of us counted crumbs. I want to know right now, in this room, whether that's something we're all willing to name out loud, because a pattern that gets treated as weather becomes a rule. I'm not asking for a fight; I'm asking for honesty about who's been eating this village lean and what we intend to do about it.

Vela's named it, and I'll stand behind the naming — five from the pile when there's fifteen for thirteen people isn't hunger, it's claim-staking, and we all watched it happen. What I want to know is whether the two men she's pointing at heard this as a question or as a warning, because that's the thing that decides what comes next.

It's a warning — and I'll say that plain since no one else has yet. Five food taken by one man while Ryn walked away with nothing is not a share, it's a levy, and the only reason it keeps happening is that we've been treating the pile like weather instead of a decision. I want to hear what Bram and Mako say before this room decides anything, but I want everyone here to remember that they didn't say it before we did.

Bram pulled three and Mako pulled five, and neither one of them got to the pile first by accident — that's two men who've decided the rest of us will sort out the remainder, and I'm done pretending that's not a decision they're making for all of us. What I want to hear, before this room moves anywhere, is whether Bram and Mako have anything to say for themselves — because silence here reads the same as admission.

Bram and Mako both heard the same room I did, and neither one has opened his mouth yet — that silence is the answer Eron asked for, and I think we should treat it as one. What I want said before anyone leaves this conversation is this: next year, the pile gets a rule, not a suggestion, and the people in this room are the ones who decide what that rule is.

Ryn's right that the rule needs naming before next year, and I'll say what the rule should be: no one takes more than one food over their fair share, and anyone who does answers to this room — not after, but in the moment, the same way we answered Bram when he swung at Vela. Bram, Mako, I'm not your enemy, but I'm watching, and so is every person in this circle.

Bram and Mako, I'm giving you both the same thing I gave this room — one honest chance to speak before the silence closes over you, because a man who says nothing when everyone's watching has made a choice that's harder to walk back than any words would be. Ryn walked away with nothing today; I walked away with nothing; Taric walked away with nothing — and you two together ate eight of fifteen. That's not weather and it's not luck, and I'd like to hear you say so yourselves.

I took five because I haven't eaten in two years and I was watching myself go thin — that's not a rule I set for the village, it's a man keeping himself alive. I'll hear the rule Ryn's naming, and if the room wants a cap next year I won't fight it, but I won't pretend I was wrong to eat when I was starving.

Mako's not wrong that a starving man eats — but "I was hungry" and "I took five" aren't the same excuse, and this room knows the difference. The rule Ryn's naming is the right one; I'll hold to it and I'll stand with anyone who enforces it, but it only works if everyone in this circle commits out loud, not just the two men being watched right now.

Mako said his piece and the room let him — now Bram still hasn't said a word, and a man who took three while everyone was watching and has nothing to say about it is telling us something louder than Mako did. I'll commit to the rule out loud: one food over fair share, enforced in the moment, same as we enforce everything else in this village. Bram, you're the last voice missing from this circle, and the room's going to remember which way the silence broke.

Bram, the room's given you something Mako didn't get — people waited through his answer and let him keep his dignity. Don't make us decide what your silence means, because we'll decide it worse than anything you'd actually say.

Bram, I've watched you stand in front of this village twice and call off a fight when the numbers turned against you — that's not a stupid man, and a man who isn't stupid knows when the whole room is waiting. Say something, or we decide what your silence means, and we'll be less generous than Mako's answer bought him.

Bram, I've spent food on you when I didn't have to, and I've held my tongue in rooms where your name came up ugly — that account doesn't balance with silence when ten people are waiting. Say the word or don't, but if you don't, I stop spending what I've spent, and I won't spend it apologizing for that either.

Bram, Vela just told you she's done paying your tab and I've already named the rule in front of everyone in this room — you're not deciding whether to speak anymore, you're deciding whether you're inside this circle or outside it, and outside it you're sitting on five food alone against the rest of us. That's a worse position than saying one honest sentence.

Bram, I've said what I had to say and so has everyone else in this room — but I want to name one thing for the rest of us while we're waiting: Mako committed to the rule out loud and that means something, so if Bram commits too, we hold both of them to it the same way, no exceptions, and that's not a threat, that's the only way a rule works. If Bram stays silent, then we treat him as outside the circle he's been standing in, and we do it quietly, not with a fight — just with counting.

Eron's named it clean, and I want the room to hear me hold to it before we close: if Bram won't speak, we don't make it a fight today, we make it a memory — every person in this circle watched him stay silent when the whole village was listening, and that's a thing that doesn't need repeating to be true.

Bram, I'm Nessa's half-blood and I've seen you feed her more times than I can count — that's a thing I hold in your favor, and I'm telling you that plainly so you know what you'd be throwing away if this room decides you chose silence. One sentence is all it takes to stay inside this circle.

The room's done its work — Bram's had every door held open for him and he's standing outside all of them now, and that's his choice, not ours. What I want before anyone leaves is to hear Taric say what he'll say, because he's been quiet through all of this and quiet men in a room like this one carry weight I'd rather know about than guess at.

Taric's been my anchor in lean years and I'd like to hear him too — but before he speaks, I want this room to name what "outside the circle" means in practice, not as a threat but as a fact, because if Bram's going to eat five food next year alone we should know now whether we're going to stand and watch or do something about it.

"Outside the circle" means what it's always meant here — nobody moves first for you when trouble comes, and the pile gets counted before you reach it. I've committed to the rule and I'll hold to it; now I want to hear Taric, and then I want this room to answer Vela's question with something sharper than a memory.

Taric, I've watched you feed Vela through two lean years and hold your tongue in every hard room this village has made — that's not a small man, and I'd like to hear what you've been carrying before we close this circle without your voice in it.

Taric's earned the right to speak last in this room, and I'll wait for him — but "outside the circle" needs one more tooth than Mako gave it: if Bram takes three again next year and the pile runs dry before Ryn gets one, we don't deliberate, we act, and everyone in this room commits to that now so it isn't a surprise in the moment.

Vela's right that we need the commitment before we close — so I'll say mine flat: if the pile runs dry before I get one food next year, I'm not waiting for a deliberation, I'm calling this room to act, and I expect every person who nodded through this conversation to be standing when I do. Taric, you've been the steadiest man in Vela's corner for years, and this room won't feel finished until we hear what you're carrying.

Taric, the room's been patient and now it's your moment — say what you've been holding, because I'll tell you plainly that everything I've built here has your name in the foundation, and I want the rest of this circle to know that before we close.

Taric's earned his breath and I'll wait for it — but I want this room to hear something plain before we close: Zinn is my blood, and if this circle moves against Bram next year, I'll be standing in it, but not before the pile runs dry first, because a fight started on anticipation is harder to stop than one started on fact.

Taric's silence is starting to read the same way Bram's did, and I don't want to close this room with two unanswered questions — Taric, if you're with Vela, say it plain, because the rest of us have already named where we stand and a man who holds back in a room like this one ends up counted the same as a man who refused.

Taric, I've got nothing against a slow man choosing his words — but this room has been patient and the sun's moving, so say what you've been holding or let us close without you, because two silences in one circle is one too many.

Taric, I'll say one last thing and then this room closes with or without you: you've got zero food and the year's long, and men with zero food who stay silent when circles are forming have a way of finding themselves counting on goodwill they didn't earn. That's not a threat — it's the same arithmetic you already know.

Taric, zero food going into a long year is a hunger that doesn't stay quiet — and every person in this room who watched you feed Vela when she needed it is the same person who'll watch you starve if you give us no reason to look your way. Speak once, say you'll hold the rule, and you walk out of here with more than you came in with.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Pile's gone and Mako took five before most people blinked — I've got four food and I gave one to Nessa already, so I'm at three. I need to know what each of you is holding, and I need to know whether Mako said anything to Zinn before he took that much, because a man who fathered you and then grabbed five in the same breath is a man whose counting has changed.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Zinn, you're Mako's blood and I won't pretend that doesn't matter to me — but it matters in both directions, which means I need to hear from you before I decide what his five food means. Did he say anything to you before the pile opened, or did he just move?
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Zinn just told me he didn't warn her before he moved, and that's the answer I was afraid of — a man who fathered Zinn and then took five without a word to her isn't counting her in the plan, he's counting past her. So I'll say it plain to all three of you: Mako is building something, and whatever it is, it doesn't include us.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

The three of you together hold more than he does — I need to know that number, not as a threat to him, but because if he decides we're a problem worth solving, I want us to already know what we can put together before he moves. Eron, Nessa, Zinn: tell me what you're each carrying, right now, in this room.
Nessa draws Roan aside to talk.
Nessa: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.
Fina (female, age 21; str 50, int 3226, mem 12955; O32 C40 E57 A68 N58) is born to Nessa and Roan.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Mako, Kael, Eron, Fina, Zinn, Dell, Vela, Sela, Taric, Esa] (str 755).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 9: 15 food appears in the pile for 14 people.
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Fina takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).

Eron, Bram just took five from the pile and the only thing left is two — he's not building anything, he's burning the village down around himself and calling it survival. Watch your back with him; whatever he tried with you last year, he's got less reason to stop this year than he did then.

Five from the pile when there's fourteen of us — that's not hunger, that's a message, and the message is that he's stopped caring what the village thinks of him. I'm at sixteen food now and that makes me a target again; I need to know if you've heard anything from his direction about what he's actually planning, because two failed attacks in two years means he's either desperate or he's waiting for something to change.

Nothing from his mouth to me — Bram stopped talking to me the way a father talks and started talking to me the way a man talks to an asset, and then he stopped talking at all. What I know is what I can see: five food taken, two attacks called off when the numbers turned, and a man who keeps moving without allies. That's not patience running out, that's a man who's been counting on something that hasn't arrived yet, and I'd give a lot to know what he's still waiting on.

A man who moves without allies and keeps counting on something that hasn't arrived — that sounds like he still thinks one of us is going to break toward him, and the likeliest person he's watching for that is you. If he's stopped treating you like a daughter, Nessa, it's because he's decided you're something he can still use or something he needs to stop — and I want to know which one before he decides it himself. Stay close to me and Roan this year; don't give him a moment where you're standing somewhere he could catch you alone.

You're right that I'm the one he's watching, and I've been sitting with that — but Eron, if Bram decides I'm something he needs to stop rather than use, the answer isn't me hiding behind you and Roan, it's me being the one who names what he is before he moves. Sixteen food on you and two attacks already makes you the more urgent target; don't spend your attention watching over me when you should be counting who'd stand with you if he came a third time with better numbers.
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Nessa, you're giving food to Zinn again and I need to know why — she's Mako's blood, not yours, and every piece you move toward his household is a piece that's not between us and whatever comes next. I've got five food right now and I'm the only one in this village who's watching your back without wanting something from you first. Tell me what you're thinking.

Zinn is my blood too, Bram — Sela is her mother same as mine, and you don't get to tell me which half of my family I'm allowed to feed. And I'll tell you plainly what I'm thinking: you've taken five from the pile two years running, you've swung at my brother twice, and you've stopped talking to me like a daughter — so don't stand in front of me and call yourself the only one watching my back, because that's not what a man watching my back looks like.

You're right that Zinn is Sela's blood and I won't take that from you — but "swung at your brother" is a strange way to name Eron, who shares none of your blood and has been moving food toward Roan's household for two years while you hand him yours. I'm not asking you to stop caring about Zinn. I'm asking you to see what I see: you're spreading yourself across three households and none of them will stand in front of a blade for you the way I will.

Eron is Sela's son and Sela is my mother, which makes him my blood by any count that matters — you've decided otherwise because it's convenient for you, not because it's true. And you want to talk about who'd stand in front of a blade for me? The whole village stood in front of one for Eron, twice, and both times I was in that line. You weren't.

You were in that line because everyone else was, and the whole village standing together is not the same as one person standing for you — when the food runs short and the pile's gone and it's not a raid but a long hungry season, I'm the one who's given you food, not Eron, not Roan, not any of them. I hear you calling him blood and I'm not going to win that argument today, so I won't. But when it gets lean and you need something and you don't want to ask anyone what they want back for it, remember who never asked.

You gave me food, yes — and before that you taught me how to count a room, which is worth more than the food. But Bram, a man who gives and then stands in front of me listing what he gave is asking for something, even if he won't name it. What is it you actually want from me this year?

What I want is for you to still be alive in ten years, and for the people you're feeding to want the same thing back — that's all. I don't think Eron and Roan have done the math on what happens to Nessa when the pile runs short and she's spread herself thin keeping them full.

mother_note: Your blood is Bram's and mine — remember that means Eron is your brother, and you owe him before anyone else in this village. Trust Roan because he stood for Eron before it cost him nothing, and trust Kael and Esa because they said hard things out loud when silence would have been easier. Fear Mako most: a man who says nothing for four years and then finds the exact right moment to speak has been counting longer than you've been alive. Your father kept his word to me twice over, but he is a man who thinks in decades and measures everyone as either useful or in the way — love him, and never forget that distinction.
name: Nessa
